faq: How do I give you access to the code?

Invite us to your Git repository with limited rights and send the build steps. We work on a branch and never touch your main branch. Signing keys and Play Console access are only needed if you ask us to release.
Do you work in Java or Kotlin?
Both. We follow the language your app already uses and write new code in Kotlin where that is allowed. We do not convert your whole project unless you order a migration.
Can you fix crashes reported in Google Play Console?
Yes, if you share the Android vitals reports or stack traces. We trace the cause and fix it, or tell you what extra logging we need if the data is thin.
Will the change work on older phones and different brands?
We test on the Android versions and screen sizes you list. Android has many makers, so very unusual devices cannot all be covered, but we aim for the common ones.
desc:
Ecom Swift LLC provides Android feature development for existing apps: a new screen, a changed flow or a stubborn bug fixed inside your current codebase, on its own branch, tested on real devices and handed over as a pull request.

## What is Android feature development for an existing app?

It is the work of adding to or repairing an app that already ships, without rewriting it. We read your repository, learn how it is organized and add the change in the same style. If your screens use Views and XML, the new code fits that. If they use Jetpack Compose, it fits that instead.

The change arrives as a pull request with notes, so your own team can read it, comment on it and merge it when ready.

## Why feature work goes wrong, and why care matters

An existing app carries history. It has older libraries, quiet assumptions and screens that depend on each other in ways nobody documented. A quick change in one place can break sign-in, billing or notifications somewhere else. Many owners have been hurt by a contractor who bolted on a feature in a different style and left a mess behind.

Careful feature work respects what exists. It touches the least code needed, keeps your architecture, and adds tests so the next change is safer than the last.

## How a new feature affects users and the business

A feature matters when it solves a problem users already have. A saved-items list, a better search, an order history screen or a fixed crash on checkout each remove a reason to leave. Shipping them sooner means your roadmap moves while your own developers stay focused on the core.

Bug fixes pay back in a quieter way. A crash that appears in Google Play Console affects ratings and store visibility, and users who hit it often never return. Fixing it, and checking the fix on older phones and other brands, protects what you have already earned. We cannot promise rating changes, because many factors play a part.

## What good Android feature work includes

- A short written brief that states what the feature does and what it must not change.
- A study of your current architecture, navigation and naming before coding.
- A separate Git branch, so your main line stays untouched until you approve.
- New screens or flows that match your design, spacing and component use.
- Connection to your existing API, with sensible handling of errors and slow networks.
- Unit tests for new logic, plus interface tests in the larger package.
- Checks on an emulator, a real phone and several Android versions.
- Analytics events for the new feature when you want them.
- Clear change notes listing every file touched and why.
- Help preparing the release bundle in the fuller package.

## How we work

You send the repository and a brief. We confirm the scope, ask about edge cases and agree how the result will be tested. The Basic package suits one small change or bug fix. Standard covers a new screen or flow connected to your API with tests across versions. Premium handles a larger feature with matching design, analytics, interface tests and release help.

Work happens in your own repository, so there is no handover of files later. If we find an unrelated problem on the way, we tell you rather than quietly widening the change.

## Dos and don'ts for smooth feature delivery

**Do:**
- Write down the exact behavior you expect, including empty and error states.
- Share design files or screenshots for any new screen.
- Tell us which devices and Android versions your users have.
- Give a person on your side the job of merging.
- Keep a build running so we can compare before and after.

**Avoid:**
- Changing the brief while the branch is open.
- Skipping the pull request notes, which help later developers.
- Asking for several unrelated features in one request.
- Forgetting that older phones may behave differently.
- Merging without trying the change on your own device.

## Who this is for

A small company with one part-time developer may need extra hands for a bigger task. A founder whose original developer left may need a new screen without a full rebuild. An agency may need a reliable pair of hands for an Android task inside a client project. Teams with crashes in their Play Console reports can also use it to clear them.

## What we need from you

Send repository access, a short brief and any API notes. Access is given by inviting us as a collaborator on your Git host, limited to the project. We never need passwords or your personal sign-ins. A test account and a short description of how to build the app save time.
